subject: Customer advisory: transient streaming responsiveness degradation and immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@gigabank.com>, Evan Turner <evan@paynet.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Customer advisory: transient streaming responsiveness degradation and immediate mitigations

Hi Sarah / Evan,

I'm writing to surface a transient degradation we began seeing at ~08:58 PDT that affected streaming/chat token delivery for a subset of customer requests (including some GigaBank sessions). Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 per-token latency and periodic stalls where clients saw multi-second gaps between token chunks.

What we're doing now (immediate mitigations):
- Per-customer fallback: we can flip an account-level setting to force non-streaming responses for GigaBank traffic while we stabilize streaming (this preserves correctness at a small UX cost). I can enable this for you immediately.
- Canary rollback of a recent batching tweak that increased kernel scheduling pressure for mid-sized sequences. We'll rollback to the prior batch policy to relieve backlog.
- Edge proxy scheduling patch to better prioritize low-latency streams; will be rolled to 10% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics look good.
- Short-term model suggestion: if you need lowest latency for interactive agents, switch to the lighter variant redwood-chat-medium-v2 (lower memory footprint, slightly lower throughput cost).
- Client guidance: reduce per-request max_tokens and chunk_size, and increase stream timeout to 10s to avoid premature client reconnection.

Attachments: incident_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook we are executing), transient_kpis_20270914.csv (early telemetry snapshot).

Impact window: we expect the initial rollback + proxy patch to begin reducing p99 latency inside ~60–90 minutes; we'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we reach baseline.

I'll enable a temporary per-account streaming fallback for GigaBank now unless you prefer us to hold — that will prevent user-facing pauses at the cost of losing incremental token streaming. If you want us to proceed, reply "Enable fallback" and we'll flip it and confirm.

Contact: I'm available on the incident Slack channel (#inc-gigabank) and by phone if you want a live bridge.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook, 1.2MB), transient_kpis_20270914.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@gigabank.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:11:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer advisory: transient streaming responsiveness degradation and immediate mitigations

Thanks for the quick heads up, Lauren.

We're seeing the behavior on our end: the agent UI stutters for roughly 5–10s on some prompts, which breaks conversational flows with our customers. We have a couple of live demos this afternoon (11:30 PT and 15:00 PT) — need to confirm whether non-streaming fallback will preserve these sessions or if we'll have to switch to a different workflow.

Two quick Qs:
1) ETA for a full restore to baseline?
2) Can you enable the per-account fallback automatically for GigaBank so we don't have to change client code mid-demo?

Appreciate the fast coordination.

—Sarah
SVP, Digital Products
GigaBank

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 09:02 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [original advisory omitted for thread brevity]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@gigabank.com>, Evan Turner <evan@paynet.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:28:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer advisory: transient streaming responsiveness degradation and immediate mitigations

Sarah —

Thanks, understood on the demo risk. We'll enable per-account non-streaming fallback for GigaBank immediately; this will cause the API to return complete payloads rather than incremental token chunks for ongoing sessions (no client code change required). I'm enabling it now and will confirm when the setting is active.

ETA and next steps:
- 09:30 PDT: feature-flag flip for GigaBank fallback (in progress).
- 09:45 PDT: start canary rollback of the batching tweak (10% of hosts).
- 10:15 PDT: edge proxy scheduling patch to 10% canary.
- 11:15 PDT: if telemetry looks stable, promote rollback + patch to 50% and re-evaluate.
- Full baseline expected within 60–90 minutes if canaries are green; worst-case remediation (full rollback + staged patch) could take up to 3 hours.

Temporary operational knobs for your team (if you want to try client-side changes before we flip fallback):
- Header: X-Redwood-Preferred-Stream: none — instructs our gateway to serve complete responses for the single request.
- Reduce input chunk_size to 512 tokens and set max_tokens <= 256 for interactive flows.
- Set client reconnection backoff to 5s to avoid spurious reconnect storms.

We just flipped the fallback for your account and I'm seeing the toggle report active in our admin console. Please confirm whether your demos can proceed; we'll keep the fallback in place until we see stable token delivery for 2 consecutive 15-minute windows.

I'll open a dedicated Slack thread and send a short postmortem within 48 hours explaining root cause and durable fixes.

—Lauren

Attachments: gigabank_fallback_mop.txt (tiny MOP showing how we flip the flag)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: GigaBank streaming latency — actions, credit proposal, and owners

Team — internal recap and action items (do not forward to customer):

Summary: we triggered a rollback + proxy patch after mid-morning telemetry showed p99 streaming latency spikes impacting interactive sessions for select customers (GigaBank among them). We enabled per-account fallback to protect their demos and reduced the immediate surface impact.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft a short follow-up email to Sarah with timeline, what we changed, and a proposed 48-hour postmortem (owner: Marissa). Due EOD today.
- Rishi: evaluate whether this incident should trigger a commercial goodwill offer (suggestion: one-month usage credit capped at $Xk). Coordinate with finance/accounting/legal. Due: 24 hours.
- Monica/Infra: run the full postmortem with the infra team; we need root-cause confirmation on whether the batching tweak or kernel scheduler interaction is primary. Include heatmap from 08:50–09:30 window. Due: 48 hours.
- Engineering: add an automatic per-customer fallback capability to our routing rules (owner: infra eng). Priority P1 for this week.

Please update the shared doc with links to logs and the exact artifact names (I started the doc here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxx/gigabank-incident-20270914).

Marissa — once your draft is ready, I'll review before you send to Sarah. Rishi — keep me posted on the commercial ask; we should not promise credits without finance/legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
